summary: A five-minute, two-source briefing on the memes, slang, people, movies, music, products, and news shaping internet culture right now.

sections.title: Memes
sections.description: The July Meme of the Month results, kept in poll order and filtered to memes Lessons in Meme Culture covered in any upload from the past two months.

sources.label: Lessons in Meme Culture · past 2 months

items.title: Jimothy the raccoon
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: Jimothy is a wild raccoon with short spine syndrome who lives in Seattle's Ballard neighborhood. Videos of Jimothy spread across social media, inspiring works of fan art, memes and viral coverage in the media and with streamers and social media stars.
items.alt: Visual example of the Jimothy the raccoon meme

items.title: Kwebbelkop Laughing / YourRAGE Laugh
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: Kwebbelkop Laughing or YourRAGE Laugh refers to a viral sound effect of YouTuber and Twitch streamer YourRAGE loudly laughing in an exaggerated manner, which is often described as sounding like Dutch YouTuber Kwebbelkop. In 2026, the laugh became a trending sound on social media as it was used in memes, often depicting both YourRAGE and Kwebbelkop in different edits.
items.alt: Kwebbelkop portrait used with the viral laughing sound

items.title: Hatsune Miku World Cup Custody Battle
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: Hatsune Miku World Cup Custody Battle is a social game, meme and fan art trend that emerged during the 2026 FIFA World Cup in which social media users jokingly treat tournament matches as battles for the "custody" of the Japanese virtual singer Hatsune Miku. The joke proposes that whichever national team defeats the previous holder earns temporary "custody" of the Vocaloid character, inspiring artists to redesign Miku in the country's colors, clothing and cultural motifs until that team is eliminated.
items.alt: Visual example of the Hatsune Miku World Cup Custody Battle meme

items.title: Mbappé Special
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: Mbappé Special is a slang term and series of memes based on a viral video of French footballer and soccer star Kylian Mbappe saying, during an interview, that the "Kylian Special" is "for example, nothing," when asked what he likes to cook. The clip of Mbappe saying the Mbappe Special is "nothing" inspired memes that use the term as slang to replace the word "nothing" over the following weeks as it spread online.
items.alt: Visual example of the Mbappé Special meme

items.title: John Rod
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: John Rod is a nickname for an unnamed stand that appears in chapter 38 of the manga series JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 9: The JOJOLands. The stand was popularized online in mid-July 2026, inspiring edits, fan art, memes and other fan content.
items.alt: John Rod from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure

moreItems.title: Stay In Character
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Stay In Character is a catchphrase and series of memes based on a scene from the 2026 Backrooms movie in which the protagonist, Clark (played by actor Chiwetel Ejiofor), yells, "Stay in character!" In June 2026, the film's scene became the subject of numerous memes on social media as the moment was used as an exploitable format with brainrot edits, recreations, Accuracy Reenactments and more.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Stay In Character meme

moreItems.title: Funky Ehh
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: We'll Drive A Funky Ehh or He'll Drive A Funky Ehh refers to a viral video of a kid claiming, during a game of Fortnite, that a remix of the song " Someone to Call My Lover " by Janet Jackson is by Oliver Tree, singing the song, "Maybe we'll meet at a bar, we'll drive a fancy ehh." A clip of the moment went viral on social media and Instagram Reels later that month, inspiring animations, remixes and memes based on the audio of the kid singing the song.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Funky Ehh meme

moreItems.title: Somebody Get These Beggars Out Of Here
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Somebody Get These Beggars Out Of Here is a quote from the character Antinous, played by actor Robert Pattinson, in Christopher Nolan's 2026 epic fantasy movie The Odyssey, which appeared online shortly after the film's release in mid-July 2026. The scene is typically used online as a simple catchphrase and reaction meme to mock someone for being poor or begging for something, with the GIF or reaction image of Pattinson from the movie also being used as an exploitable in which creators add different visual elements to him.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Somebody Get These Beggars Out Of Here meme

moreItems.title: Homer Let the Barts Out
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Homer Let the Barts Out is a brainrot and AI song by Rabadoonga about Homer Simpson letting a massive group of Bart Simpsons out of the house, who go on to cause uncontrollable destruction. It inspired memes on sites including social media, X / Twitter and Instagram Reels, including lip dubs, animations, covers and AI-generated videos.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Homer Let the Barts Out meme

moreItems.title: Best of Zach
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Best Of Zach refers to a series of memes about the Oney Plays video "Best Of Zach" and its thumbnail, which shows a cartoon drawing of Zach, also known as PsychicPebbles, over a pink background. In June 2026, a video that animates the video and sets it to an amateur rap song that repeats the words "best of Zach" was popularized online, inspiring further "Best Of Zach" memes.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Best of Zach meme

sections.eyebrow: Annual slang review · by page views
sections.title: Slang
sections.description: Terms from Know Your Meme's annual slang review, ranked from most to least lifetime views on their Know Your Meme entries and checked against Urban Dictionary.

sources.label: Know Your Meme · annual slang review

items.title: 67 / six-seven
items.subtitle: A deliberately ambiguous number catchphrase
items.description: A call-and-response built around saying “six-seven,” often with a palms-up gesture. Its lack of one fixed meaning is the joke, so people use it as a deliberately contextless reply.
items.alt: The number 67 as used in the six-seven meme

items.title: Dead Rose Emoji
items.subtitle: The wilted rose used as ironic punctuation
items.description: The wilted rose emoji 🥀 became an ironic alternative to the broken-heart emoji. People append it to dramatic, embarrassing, disappointed, or mock-heartbroken remarks.
items.alt: Visual example of Dead Rose Emoji

items.title: Aura farming
items.subtitle: Performing effortless cool for status
items.description: Aura farming means doing something calculated to look effortlessly cool and build imaginary social status. The phrase captions dramatic entrances, poses, edits, and knowingly over-styled behavior.
items.alt: Stylized scene representing aura farming

items.title: SYBAU
items.subtitle: An aggressive request to be quiet
items.description: SYBAU expands to “shut your bitch ass up.” It is used as a blunt dismissal or exaggerated reaction, often as an acronym so the punchline lands only after someone decodes it.
items.alt: Reaction image associated with the acronym SYBAU

items.title: Labubu Matcha Dubai Chocolate
items.subtitle: A pileup of 2025 consumer-trend buzzwords
items.description: Labubu is a toothy collectible toy, matcha is a powdered green-tea drink, and Dubai chocolate is a pistachio-filled chocolate bar. Stringing them together parodies algorithm-driven consumer trends.
items.alt: Visual example of Labubu Matcha Dubai Chocolate

moreItems.title: Clanker
moreItems.subtitle: A derogatory word for robots
moreItems.description: A Star Wars insult for battle droids that returned as a joking slur for robots and AI. People use it to mock a machine, chatbot, or conspicuously automated behavior.
moreItems.alt: A battle droid associated with the slang term clanker

moreItems.title: TS PMO ICL
moreItems.subtitle: An intentionally overloaded slang acronym
moreItems.description: TS PMO ICL expands to “this shit pisses me off, I can’t lie.” People use it sincerely, or pile it into deliberately overloaded captions that parody compressed internet slang.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of TS PMO ICL

moreItems.title: Performative Male
moreItems.subtitle: Someone visibly curating an appealing persona
moreItems.description: A performative male conspicuously reads feminist books, drinks matcha, carries a tote bag, or wears wired earbuds to appear sensitive and attractive. The label mocks an obviously curated personality.

moreItems.title: Chopped
moreItems.subtitle: Unattractive, damaged, or badly done
moreItems.description: Calling someone or something “chopped” means it looks unattractive, damaged, or badly put together. It appears in blunt reactions, appearance jokes, and before-and-after comparisons.
moreItems.alt: Reaction image associated with chopped slang

sections.title: People
sections.description: Last month's most-viewed English Wikipedia pages that represent living people, excluding politicians and allowing at most two people from each broad primary category.

items.title: Erling Haaland
items.subtitle: Sports
items.description: Erling Braut Haaland (born 21 July 2000) is a Norwegian professional footballer who plays as a striker for Premier League club Manchester City and the Norway national team. Regarded as one of the best players in the world and the greatest Norwegian player of all time, he is known for his speed, strength, positioning, and finishing inside the box.
items.alt: Portrait of Erling Haaland

items.title: Lamine Yamal
items.subtitle: Sports
items.description: Lamine Yamal Nasraoui Ebana (born 13 July 2007), commonly known as Lamine Yamal, is a Spanish professional footballer who plays as a right winger for the La Liga club Barcelona and the Spain national team. He is widely regarded as one of the best players in the world.
items.alt: Portrait of Lamine Yamal

items.title: Christopher Nolan
items.subtitle: Film
items.description: Sir Christopher Edward Nolan (born 30 July 1970) is a British and American filmmaker. Known for his Hollywood blockbusters with complex storytelling, Nolan is considered a leading filmmaker of the 21st century.
items.alt: Portrait of Christopher Nolan

items.title: Zendaya
items.subtitle: Film
items.description: Zendaya Maree Stoermer Coleman ( zen-DAY-ə; born September 1, 1996), known mononymously as Zendaya, is an American actress and singer-songwriter. Her accolades include two Primetime Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe.
items.alt: Portrait of Zendaya

items.title: Shakira
items.subtitle: Music
items.description: Shakira Isabel Mebarak Ripoll ( shə-KEER-ə, Spanish: [ʃaˈkiɾa isaˈβel meβaˈɾak riˈpol]; born 2 February 1977), known mononymously as Shakira, is a Colombian singer-songwriter, dancer, and record producer. Referred to as the "Queen of Latin Music", she has had a significant impact on the musical landscape of Latin America and has been credited with popularizing Hispanophone music globally, contributing to…
items.alt: Portrait of Shakira

moreItems.title: Sonam Wangchuk
moreItems.subtitle: Science & technology
moreItems.description: Sonam Wangchuk (born 1966) is an Indian engineer, educator, and activist. He is the founding director of the Students' Educational and Cultural Movement of Ladakh (SECMOL), which was founded in 1988 by a group of students who struggled with the public education system.

moreItems.title: Taylor Swift
moreItems.subtitle: Music
moreItems.description: Taylor Alison Swift (born December 13, 1989) is an American singer-songwriter. One of the most influential figures in popular culture, Swift is known for her autobiographical songwriting and artistic reinventions.

moreItems.title: Jeff Bezos
moreItems.subtitle: Business
moreItems.description: Jeffrey Preston Bezos ( BAY-zohss; né Jorgensen; born January 12, 1964) is an American businessman, and the founder, executive chairman, and former president and CEO of Amazon, the world's largest e-commerce and cloud computing company. According to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index and Forbes, he was the world's wealthiest person from 2017 to 2021, and in 2026 his net worth was approximately US$284 billion.

moreItems.title: Andrew Tate
moreItems.subtitle: Business
moreItems.description: Emory Andrew Tate III (born 1 December 1986) is an American and British social media personality and former professional kickboxer who built a webcam pornography business before gaining notoriety for promoting various highly controversial positions in the manosphere. His commentary has resulted in his expulsion from various social media platforms and concern that he promotes misogynistic views to his audience.

moreItems.title: Amelia Dimoldenberg
moreItems.subtitle: Media
moreItems.description: Amelia Dimoldenberg ( dim-OHL-dən-burg; born 30 January 1994) is an English comedian, writer, and presenter. She is the creator and host of the web series Chicken Shop Date, in which she interviews celebrities in fried chicken restaurants while subjecting them to her sarcastic, deadpan, and awkward sense of humour.

sections.title: Movies
sections.description: Movie pages from last month's English Wikipedia topviews, kept in descending page-view order. IMDb ratings are shown as context but do not affect rank.

items.title: The Odyssey
items.subtitle: 2026 film
items.description: The Odyssey is a 2026 epic action fantasy film written and directed by Christopher Nolan, who produced it with his wife Emma Thomas. An adaptation of Homer's ancient Greek epic poem the Odyssey, it stars an ensemble cast including Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong'o, Zendaya, and Charlize Theron.
items.alt: The Odyssey 2026 theatrical poster

items.title: Obsession
items.subtitle: 2025 film
items.description: Obsession is a 2025 American supernatural horror film written, directed, and edited by Curry Barker. The film follows Bear (Michael Johnston), a music store employee who buys a supernatural toy that grants his wish for his friend Nikki (Inde Navarrette) to fall in love with him, which makes her become obsessed.
items.alt: Obsession poster or lead image

items.title: Project Hail Mary
items.subtitle: 2026 film
items.description: Project Hail Mary is a 2026 science fiction film produced and directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller and written by Drew Goddard, based on the 2021 novel Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir. It stars Ryan Gosling, who also produced the film, as Ryland Grace; Sandra Hüller, James Ortiz, and Lionel Boyce play supporting roles.
items.alt: Project Hail Mary poster or lead image

items.title: Backrooms
items.subtitle: 2026 film
items.description: Backrooms is a 2026 American science fiction psychological horror film directed and co-scored by Kane Parsons (in his feature directorial debut), and written by Will Soodik. It is based on Parsons's web series which was inspired by the "Backrooms" creepypasta.
items.alt: Backrooms poster or lead image

items.title: Alpha
items.subtitle: Movie
items.description: Alpha is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language action thriller film directed by Shiv Rawail, in his feature film debut, and produced by Aditya Chopra under Yash Raj Films. Written by Soumil Shukla, Shridhar Raghavan, Ishita Moitra and Uday Chopra, it is the seventh installment in the YRF Spy Universe and the first female-led film in the universe, starring Alia Bhatt, Sharvari, Anil Kapoor and Bobby Deol.
items.alt: Alpha poster or lead image

moreItems.title: Supergirl
moreItems.subtitle: 2026 film
moreItems.description: Supergirl is a 2026 American superhero film based on the DC Comics superheroine Kara Zor-El / Supergirl. Directed by Craig Gillespie and written by Ana Nogueira, it is the second film in the DC Universe (DCU).

moreItems.title: Jana Nayagan
moreItems.subtitle: Movie
moreItems.description: Jana Nayagan (Tamil pronunciation: [dʑanaː n̪aːjagan]; transl. People's Hero) is a 2026 Indian Tamil-language action drama film directed by H. Vinoth and produced by Venkat K. Narayana under KVN Productions. The film stars C. Joseph Vijay, Bobby Deol, Pooja Hegde, and Mamitha Baiju in the lead role alongside Nassar, Prakash Raj, Gautham Vasudev Menon, Narain, and Priyamani.
moreItems.alt: Jana Nayagan poster or lead image

moreItems.title: Evil Dead Burn
moreItems.subtitle: 2026 film
moreItems.description: Evil Dead Burn is a 2026 American supernatural horror film written and directed by Sébastien Vaniček, who co-wrote it with Florent Bernard, and produced by Rob Tapert and series creator Sam Raimi. It serves as a sequel to Evil Dead Rise (2023) and is the sixth installment in the Evil Dead film series.

moreItems.title: Masters of the Universe
moreItems.subtitle: 2026 film
moreItems.description: Masters of the Universe (also known as He-Man and the Masters of the Universe in some territories) is a 2026 American sword-and-sorcery film based on the media franchise by Mattel. It is the second live-action film adaptation after the 1987 film.
moreItems.alt: Masters of the Universe poster or lead image

moreItems.title: Toy Story 5
moreItems.subtitle: 2026 film
moreItems.description: Toy Story 5 is a 2026 American animated comedy-drama film produced by Pixar Animation Studios for Walt Disney Pictures. Directed by Andrew Stanton and written by Stanton and Kenna Harris, it is the fifth main installment in the Toy Story film series and the sequel to Toy Story 4 (2019).
